# 2 Samuel 16 — Disagreement Log
**Chapter:** 2 Samuel 16 (23 verses)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA
**Total disagreements logged:** 10

---

## V.2 — "faint" vs. "grow faint" vs. "collapses from exhaustion"
- **EMET:** "the-faint [yya'ef]"
- **LOGOS:** "those who grow faint"
- **PNEUMA:** "anyone who collapses from exhaustion"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "those who grow faint" — accurate to *ya'ef* without PNEUMA's intensification.

---

## V.3 — "son of your master" vs. "your master's grandson"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "your master's son"
- **PNEUMA:** "your master's grandson"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "your master's son" — preserves the Hebrew relational term *ben adonekha* without over-specifying genealogy.

---

## V.5 — "coming out and cursing" vs. "cursing continually" vs. "hurling curses nonstop"
- **EMET:** "coming-out, coming-out and-cursing"
- **LOGOS:** "cursing continually"
- **PNEUMA:** "hurling curses nonstop"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "cursing continually" — captures continuous participle and emphatic doubling without colloquialism.

---

## V.7 — "man of worthlessness" vs. "worthless man" vs. "scoundrel"
- **EMET:** "man of-the-worthless [beliyya'al]"
- **LOGOS:** "worthless man"
- **PNEUMA:** "scoundrel"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "worthless man" — *beliyya'al* carries connotations too severe for "scoundrel."

---

## V.8 — "in your evil" vs. "your ruin is upon you" vs. "ruined!"
- **EMET:** "behold-you in-your-evil [ra'ah]"
- **LOGOS:** "your ruin is upon you"
- **PNEUMA:** "Look at you now — ruined!"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "your ruin is upon you" — *ra'ah* means both evil and ruin/disaster; LOGOS captures the declaration formally.

---

## V.10 — "What is to me and to you" vs. "What have I to do with you" vs. "not your concern"
- **EMET:** "What [is]-to-me and-to-you"
- **LOGOS:** "What have I to do with you"
- **PNEUMA:** "This is not your concern"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "What have I to do with you" — traditional rendering of *mah-li ve-lakhem*, a recognized formula of disassociation.

---

## V.12 — Ketiv "his eye" vs. Qere "my affliction"
- **EMET:** Notes both, translates Ketiv
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** Follow Qere
- **SOPHIA ruling:** Follow Qere "my affliction" (*be'on'yi*) — more coherent reading, consistent with lament psalm theology.

---

## V.13 — "threw dust" vs. "flinging dust" vs. "kicking up clouds of dust"
- **EMET:** "threw-dust"
- **LOGOS:** "flinging dust"
- **PNEUMA:** "kicking up clouds of dust"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "flinging dust" — PNEUMA adds "clouds of" and changes the action; the Hebrew is simply *'iffer be'afar*.

---

## V.17 — "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "loyalty" for chesed
- **EMET:** "covenant-faithfulness [chesed]"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "loyalty"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "loyalty" — in this interpersonal context, *chesed* functions as personal fidelity rather than theological covenant-faithfulness. Footnote warranted.

---

## V.21 — "made yourself odious" vs. "made yourself repulsive"
- **EMET/LOGOS:** "odious"
- **PNEUMA:** "repulsive"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "odious" — hithpael of *ba'ash* is social/political offensiveness, not physical revulsion.

---
*— SOPHIA*
